title: Containment Configuration Guide for Amazon GuardDuty

blocks.text: This configuration guide provides information on prerequisites and how to integrate Zscaler ITDR with Amazon GuardDuty to contain and isolate detected attackers.

With this integration, ITDR strengthens cloud security by automatically preventing known attacker IP addresses from accessing AWS resources. When ITDR detects malicious activity, it sends the source IP address to the Amazon GuardDuty threat list. Amazon GuardDuty then uses this information to block or flag any traffic originating from these IP addresses, helping to reduce the risk of compromise and enhance threat response across your AWS environment.
Before you configure Amazon GuardDuty, ensure that you have:

blocks.item: AWS accounts with Amazon GuardDuty enabled.
Obtained the Detector ID for each region within an AWS account that must be protected.

blocks.heading: Configuring Containment Integration with Amazon GuardDuty

blocks.text: Follow these steps to integrate Amazon GuardDuty:

blocks.item: Step 1: Configure the Containment Integration Between ITDR and Amazon GuardDuty
Sign in to the AWS Management Console.
Click your username in the top-right corner.
Copy the 12-digit account ID displayed in the drop-down menu.
See image.
Ensure that the proper region is selected and go to the GuardDuty service.
In the left-side navigation, click Settings and copy the Detector ID.
See image.
Ensure that you copy Detector IDs for all accounts and regions must be protected from malicious IP addresses.
In Zscaler ITDR Admin Portal, go to Orchestrate > Containment.
In the table, locate AWS Guard Duty (Attacker IPs) and click the Edit icon.
See image.
In the AWS Guard Duty (Attacker IPs) configuration window:
Enabled: Select to enable the containment integration.
Click Add to enter the following details of an AWS account:
Name: Enter a name for the account.
AWS Account ID: Enter the account ID copied from the AWS Management Console.
Region: Select the region for the AWS account that you want to protect from malicious IP addresses.
Detector ID: Enter the detector ID for the specific region copied from the AWS Management Console.
See image.
Ensure that you have configured all accounts and regions with the respective Detector IDs.
Click Save.
The message indicating GuardDuty is ready appears along with the Show Commands option.
Click Show Commands.
See image.
Copy each command to create a role, an access permission for the role, an S3 bucket to store the threat IP address list, and a policy to allow the role to access the S3 bucket.
See image.
Go to AWS Management Console and launch AWS CloudShell for each region and run the commands.
The required role, access permissions, S3 bucket, and policies are created.
Step 2: Configure Orchestration Rule or Manually to Contain Detected Attackers
You can contain detected attackers automatically by creating an orchestration rule or manually from the Investigate page.
Create a rule.
Go to Orchestrate > Rule.
Click Add Rule.
See image.
In the Rule Details window:
Enter the name of the rule.
Select Enabled.
Create a rule using queries and conditions.
See image.
Under Respond > AWS Guard Duty.
Select Enabled.
Select the name of the Amazon GuardDuty account.
See image.
Click Save.
The attackers' IP addresses are added to the Amazon GuardDuty's Threat IP list, and any traffic originating from the IP address is blocked by AWS.
Take action from the Investigate page.
On the Investigate page, click an attack icon on the alert graph.
The event details pane opens.
Click Actions.
See image.
A list of actions that you can take to remediate the threat appears.
Click Contain with AWS Guard Duty.
See image.
In the Contain with AWS Guard Duty window, select the AWS account name from the Name drop-down menu, and click Contain.
See image.
The attackers' IP addresses are added to the Amazon GuardDuty's Threat IP list, and any traffic originating from the IP address is blocked by AWS.

blocks.text: After containing the detected attackers, you can view the details of the attacker.
